input.reasoning:
Total backlog = 202 story points across 24 tasks. With only one placeholder role (Team member, 1 FTE, $75/hr) staffing the entire project, capacity is the dominant constraint, not skill mix. I estimated effort by converting story points to hours using a common heuristic of ~8 hours per point for a single generalist (covers analysis, build, test, deploy, since there is no separation of roles like QA/PM/designer in the rate card). This gives 202 points x 8 hours = 1,616 hours of raw work.

Because there is only 1 FTE (Team member) available at 40 hours/week, this backlog represents roughly 40 weeks (~9-10 months) of solo full-time work just to build everything, before accounting for vacation, meetings, defect-fixing, or unplanned work. I flagged this capacity mismatch explicitly as an assumption/risk.

I built the labour line as a single 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour, with hours = 1,616 (full backlog) for the baseline scenario, and lower hours for reduced-scope scenarios. Since this is the only role permitted by the rate card, all labour must be attributed to it; I did not invent PM, QA, designer, etc. roles.

Non-labour costs: no infrastructure/tooling costs were specified, so I added a conservative estimate for cloud hosting/staging environment (small, since PW-1 already covers pipeline setup labour) and a placeholder for third-party services (Stripe fees are transactional, not build cost, so excluded from build budget; but I included a small allowance for tooling licenses, e.g. CI/CD, observability tooling, staging infra) as an explicit assumption-based estimate, clearly flagged as indicative.

Priority breakdown: I summed story points by priority tier and converted to dollars using the same 8 hrs/point x $75/hr rate, to show relative weight of Urgent/High/Medium/Low priority work.

Scenarios: 
- P50 (most likely): full backlog at 8 hrs/point, single FTE, no descoping = ~$121,200 labour + non-labour.
- P80 (conservative/buffer): add 20% contingency for unknowns given no historical actuals and thin staffing = ~$145,000+.
- P20 (optimistic / descoped): assume Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24 = 39 points) are deferred, reducing scope by ~19%, and some efficiency gained if hours/point drops to 7 with tooling reuse (design system, CI) = lower total.

Reductions: I identified concrete descope/defer opportunities among Low and some Medium priority items, and flagged the single-FTE constraint as the biggest lever for reducing cost (accepting longer timeline instead of adding cost, or vice versa hiring more FTEs increases cost but not shown here since rate card only has one role).

Key caveats stated in assumptions: rate card is placeholder (all costs indicative until real roles/rates assigned), no historical actuals exist, single FTE capacity vs 202-point backlog is a major schedule/cost risk, and hours-per-point ratio is an estimate absent real velocity data.</reasoning>

assumptions: Rate card is a placeholder: the single 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE does not reflect real team composition (no PM, QA, designer, backend/frontend split etc. have been defined yet). All costs are indicative only until actual roles and hourly rates are assigned to team members.

No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project; the 8 hours-per-story-point conversion used here is an industry-standard heuristic for a single generalist covering analysis, build, test and deployment, not a calibrated figure.

Only 1 FTE is available under the current rate card to deliver 202 story points of backlog (24 tasks). At 8 hrs/point this is ~1,616 hours of work, i.e. roughly 40 weeks (~9-10 months) of solo full-time effort excluding leave, meetings, defects and rework. This is a major capacity/schedule risk that should be resolved by either adding headcount (increasing cost) or accepting an extended timeline; the estimate assumes the latter (single FTE, extended schedule) since no additional roles are staffed.

Story points are assumed to scale roughly linearly to effort hours across tasks of varying complexity (e.g. legacy data migration PW-8 at 21 points is assumed proportionally larger than a 5-point task), which may not hold exactly for highly technical items like PW-8 or PW-7.

Non-labour costs (hosting, tooling licenses, third-party service setup) are rough placeholder estimates since no infrastructure budget or vendor quotes were provided; they should be replaced with real quotes once services are selected.
Stripe/payment provider transaction fees are excluded from this build-cost estimate as they are ongoing operational costs tied to revenue, not one-off delivery cost.
Priority breakdown dollar figures are derived by applying the same 8 hrs/point x $75/hr conversion to the total points in each priority tier, for relative comparison only.

reductions.description: Defer all Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase — 39 points total
reductions.effect: Removes ~19% of backlog scope from initial delivery; legacy portal can be decommissioned after go-live, admin/analytics tooling can follow customer-facing launch.

reductions.description: Descope Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) to launch with USD only, add EUR/PLN in a later iteration
reductions.effect: Removes FX-rate integration and multi-currency settlement complexity from critical path; single-currency launch is simpler to test and ship.

reductions.description: Reduce Legacy data migration scope (PW-8, 21 points) by migrating only active accounts (last 24 months) initially, archiving the rest for on-demand migration
reductions.effect: Cuts migration validation and reconciliation effort roughly in half by shrinking the initial dataset; remaining records migrated post-launch as needed.

reductions.description: Combine Audit log (PW-10) and Observability/tracing (PW-22) delivery into a single workstream reusing the same logging infrastructure
reductions.effect: Avoids duplicated setup of log pipelines/storage; both features consume the same underlying event stream.

reductions.description: Defer Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA (PW-15, 8 points) until after initial customer-facing launch, doing only critical keyboard/contrast fixes at launch
reductions.effect: Full audit and remediation across all screens moved to a fast-follow release; reduces risk of it blocking launch but must be scheduled before any compliance deadline.

reductions.description: Resolve the single-FTE capacity constraint by clarifying real team composition and rates before committing to a fixed-price bid; avoids costly change orders later
reductions.effect: Not a direct dollar saving but prevents cost overrun risk from an unrealistic 1-person plan; strongly recommended before finalizing any quote to Northwind Ltd.
